title: Kenyan Beef Ribs
community: Urban Kenya — the restaurant BBQ showpiece
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Beef Ribs — a full rack of beef ribs slow-roasted for 3 hours until falling-tender, finished over charcoal with a Kenyan spice rub and honey glaze. The ultimate restaurant BBQ statement — bones sticking up from a magnificent rack.
longDesc: Kenyan beef ribs — properly done — are one of the most impressive dishes in the restaurant repertoire. The three-hour slow roast followed by charcoal finishing creates meat that falls from the bone while still holding a magnificent charred exterior.
steps: Apply dry rub all over the ribs. Refrigerate 4 hours minimum.
Preheat oven to 150°C. Wrap ribs tightly in foil.
Slow roast for 2.5—3 hours until meat pulls back from bones and is very tender.
Remove ribs from foil. Brush with honey glaze.
Grill over charcoal or under broiler for 8—10 minutes, basting every 3 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes. Cut between bones to serve.
chefTips: The two-stage cooking is the secret — slow oven makes them tender; grill makes them magnificent.
Wrap tightly in foil — the steam inside creates falling-off-the-bone tenderness.
Apply glaze in multiple layers during the final grilling.
cookingScience: At 150°C over 3 hours, collagen in the rib connective tissue slowly converts to gelatin — this is the low-and-slow BBQ principle. The resulting meat is simultaneously tender and moist because the collagen conversion creates a self-basting effect. The subsequent high-heat grill creates Maillard browning impossible at low temperature.
sustainabilityTips: Beef ribs use a section of the carcass that is often underutilised — a sustainable choice.
culturalNote: Beef ribs at a Nairobi restaurant represent the ambition of Kenya's food service industry — a technically demanding dish executed with confidence, using Kenya's excellent beef to its absolute maximum potential.
